title.zh: 卷五十 列傳第三十一 文二王 明七王
title.en: Volume 50 Biographies 31: Emperor Wen's Two Princes, Emperor Ming's Seven Princes
title.raw: 卷五十 列傳第三十一 文二王 明七王 Volume 50 Biographies 31: Emperor Wen's Two Princes, Emperor Ming's Seven Princes

sentences.zh: 南齊書卷五十‧列傳第三十一

translations.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 50 · Biographies 31
translations.idiomatic: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 50 · Biographies 31

sentences.zh: 文二王 明七王

translations.literal: Wen's Two Princes; Ming's Seven Princes
translations.idiomatic: The Two Princes of Emperor Wen; The Seven Princes of Emperor Ming

sentences.zh: 文惠太子四男：安皇后生鬱林王昭業；

translations.literal: Crown Prince Wen Hui had four sons: Empress An bore the Prince of Yulin, Zhaoye;
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Wen Hui had four sons: Empress An gave birth to Zhaoye, Prince of Yulin;

sentences.zh: 宮人許氏生海陵恭王昭文；

translations.literal: the palace woman Lady Xu bore the Prince Gong of Hailing, Zhaowen;
translations.idiomatic: the palace woman Lady Xu bore Zhaowen, Prince Gong of Hailing;

sentences.zh: 陳氏生巴陵王昭秀；

translations.literal: Lady Chen bore the Prince of Baling, Zhaoxiu;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chen bore Zhaoxiu, Prince of Baling;

sentences.zh: 褚氏生桂陽王昭粲。

translations.literal: Lady Chu bore the Prince of Guiyang, Zhaocan.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chu bore Zhaocan, Prince of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 巴陵王昭秀字懷尚，太子第三子也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Baling, Zhaoxiu, style name Huaishang, was the crown prince's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoxiu, Prince of Baling, whose style name was Huaishang, was Crown Prince Wen Hui's third son.

sentences.zh: 永明中，封曲江公，千五百戶。

translations.literal: During the Yongming era he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qujiang with fifteen hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongming era he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qujiang with a fief of fifteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 十年，爲寧朔將軍、濟陽太守。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was made General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 鬱林卽位，封臨海郡王，二千戶。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yulin acceded, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Linhai Commandery with two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yulin took the throne, Zhaoxiu was enfeoffed as Prince of Linhai with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，爲使持節、都督荊雍益寧梁南北秦七州軍事、西中郎將、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang he was made Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of Military Affairs for the seven provinces of Jing, Yong, Yi, Ning, Liang, and Northern and Southern Qin, General of the West, and Governor of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longchang (494) he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Area Commander of Jing, Yong, Yi, Ning, Liang, and Northern and Southern Qin, General of the West, and Governor of Jing.

sentences.zh: 延興元年，徵爲車騎將軍，衞京師，以永嘉王昭粲代之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanxing he was summoned as General of the Chariots and Cavalry to guard the capital, and the Prince of Yongjia, Zhaocan, was sent to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanxing (494) he was recalled as General of the Chariots and Cavalry to guard the capital, and Zhaocan, Prince of Yongjia, replaced him.

sentences.zh: 明帝建武二年，通直常侍庾曇隆啓曰：「周定雒邑，天子置畿內之民；

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu under Emperor Ming, Regular Attendant Yu Tanlong submitted: "When the Zhou fixed their capital at Luoyi, the Son of Heaven placed the people of the capital domain;
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianwu (495), Regular Attendant Yu Tanlong memorialized: "When the Zhou fixed their capital at Luoyi, the Son of Heaven settled the people of the capital domain;

sentences.zh: 漢都咸陽，三輔爲社稷之衞。

translations.literal: when Han made its capital at Xianyang, the Three Metropolises were the guard of the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: when Han made its capital at Xianyang, the Three Metropolitans guarded the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 中晉南遷，事移威弛，近郡名邦，多有國食。

translations.literal: When mid-Jin moved south, affairs shifted and authority slackened; famous commanderies near the capital often received state stipends.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin moved south, authority slackened over time, and famous nearby commanderies often drew state stipends.

sentences.zh: 宋武創業，依擬古典，神州部內，不復別封。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Song founded the dynasty, following ancient models, within the imperial domain he no longer enfeoffed separately.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Song founded the dynasty on ancient models, he ceased granting separate fiefs within the imperial domain.

sentences.zh: 而孝武末年，分樹寵子，苟申私愛，有乖訓准。

translations.literal: But in the late years of Emperor Xiaowu, enfeoffments were divided to favor beloved sons, indulging private affection against proper norms.
translations.idiomatic: But in Emperor Xiaowu's later years, favored sons were enfeoffed separately to indulge private affection, contrary to proper norms.

sentences.zh: 隆昌之元，特開母弟之貴，竊謂非古。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang, special honor was opened to younger brothers of the same mother; I privately consider this uncanonical.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longchang, special rank was granted to younger uterine brothers; I submit that this is uncanonical.

sentences.zh: 聖明御宇，禮舊爲先，畿內限斷，宜遵昔制，賜茅授土，一出外州。」

translations.literal: The sage and enlightened ruler governs the realm; ancient rites come first. The limits of the capital domain should follow former institutions—bestowal of estates and grant of land should all go to outer provinces."
translations.idiomatic: The sage ruler governs the realm with ancient rites foremost; the limits of the capital domain should follow former institutions, and grants of fief and land should all lie outside the inner provinces."

sentences.zh: 詔付尚書詳議。

translations.literal: An edict referred the memorial to the Masters of Writing for detailed deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict referred the matter to the Masters of Writing for detailed deliberation.

sentences.zh: 其冬，改封昭秀爲巴陵王。

translations.literal: That winter Zhaoxiu's enfeoffment was changed to Prince of Baling.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Zhaoxiu was reassigned as Prince of Baling.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年見殺，年十六。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai he was killed. He was sixteen.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongtai (498) he was put to death at the age of sixteen.

sentences.zh: 桂陽王昭粲，太子第四子也。

translations.literal: Zhaocan, Prince of Guiyang, was the crown prince's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaocan, Prince of Guiyang, was Crown Prince Wen Hui's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 鬱林立，以皇弟封永嘉郡王，南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: When Yulin was established, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yongjia Commandery as the emperor's younger brother and made Governor of Southern Xu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yulin was installed as emperor, Zhaocan was enfeoffed as Prince of Yongjia as the emperor's younger brother and appointed Governor of Southern Xu.

sentences.zh: 延興元年，出爲使持節、都督荊雍益寧梁南北秦七州軍事、西中郎將、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanxing he went out as Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of Military Affairs for the seven provinces of Jing, Yong, Yi, Ning, Liang, and Northern and Southern Qin, General of the West, and Governor of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanxing (494) he was sent out as Bearer of the Staff, Area Commander of Jing, Yong, Yi, Ning, Liang, and Northern and Southern Qin, General of the West, and Governor of Jing.

sentences.zh: 明帝立，欲以聞喜公遙欣爲荊州，轉昭粲爲右將軍，中書令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming was established, wishing to make the Duke of Wenxi, Yaoxin, Governor of Jing, he transferred Zhaocan to General of the Right and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, intending to appoint Yaoxin, Duke of Wenxi, to Jing Province, he reassigned Zhaocan as General of the Right and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，改封桂陽王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu his enfeoffment was changed to Prince of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianwu (495) he was reassigned as Prince of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷太常，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Grand Minister of Ceremonies; his generalship remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (497) he was promoted to Grand Minister of Ceremonies, retaining his rank as general.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年見殺，年八歲。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai he was killed. He was eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongtai (498) he was put to death at the age of eight.

sentences.zh: 明帝十一男：敬皇后生東昏侯寶卷，江夏王寶玄，鄱陽王寶寅，和帝；

translations.literal: Emperor Ming had eleven sons: Empress Jing bore the Marquis of Donghun, Bao Juan, the Prince of Jiangxia, Bao Xuan, the Prince of Poyang, Bao Yin, and the Emperor He;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming had eleven sons: Empress Jing bore Bao Juan, Marquis of Donghun; Bao Xuan, Prince of Jiangxia; Bao Yin, Prince of Poyang; and the Emperor He;

sentences.zh: 殷貴嬪生巴陵隱王寶義，晉熙王寶嵩；

translations.literal: the Honored Consort Yin bore the Prince Yin of Baling, Bao Yi, and the Prince of Jinxing, Bao Song;
translations.idiomatic: Honored Consort Yin bore Bao Yi, Prince Yin of Baling, and Bao Song, Prince of Jinxing;

sentences.zh: 袁貴妃生廬陵王寶源；

translations.literal: the Honored Consort Yuan bore the Prince of Luling, Bao Yuan;
translations.idiomatic: Honored Consort Yuan bore Bao Yuan, Prince of Luling;

sentences.zh: 管淑妃生邵陵王寶攸；

translations.literal: the Virtuous Consort Guan bore the Prince of Shaoling, Bao You;
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous Consort Guan bore Bao You, Prince of Shaoling;

sentences.zh: 許淑媛生桂陽王寶貞。

translations.literal: the Lady of Graceful Demeanor Xu bore the Prince of Guiyang, Bao Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Lady of Graceful Demeanor Xu bore Bao Zhen, Prince of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 餘皆早夭。

translations.literal: The rest all died young.
translations.idiomatic: All the others died in infancy.

sentences.zh: 巴陵隱王寶義字智勇，明帝長子也。

translations.literal: The Prince Yin of Baling, Bao Yi, style name Zhiyong, was Emperor Ming's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Yi, Prince Yin of Baling, whose style name was Zhiyong, was Emperor Ming's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 本名明基。

translations.literal: His original name was Mingji.
translations.idiomatic: His original name had been Mingji.

sentences.zh: 建武元年，爲持節、都督揚南徐州軍事、前將軍、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianwu, he was made Bearer of Credentials, Supervisor of Military Affairs for Yang and Southern Xu Provinces, General of the Van, and Governor of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianwu (494), he was appointed Bearer of Credentials, Area Commander of Yang and Southern Xu, General of the Van, and Governor of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 封晉安郡王，三千戶。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Jin'an Commandery with three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Jin'an with a fief of three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 寶義少有廢疾，不堪出人閒，故止加除授，仍以始安王遙光代之。

translations.literal: Bao Yi from youth had a crippling ailment and could not bear to go out among people; therefore he received only titular appointments, and the Prince of Shi'an, Yaoguang, was sent to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Bao Yi suffered a disabling illness and could not appear in public; he therefore received only nominal appointments, while the Prince of Shi'an, Yaoguang, was sent to take his place.

sentences.zh: 轉寶義爲右將軍，領兵置佐，鎮石頭。

translations.literal: Bao Yi was transferred to General of the Right, with troops and staff assigned, garrisoning Stone City.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Yi was reassigned as General of the Right with troops and staff under him, and garrisoned Stone City.

sentences.zh: 二年，出爲使持節、都督南徐州軍事、鎮北將軍、南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year, he went out as Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of Military Affairs for Southern Xu Province, General Who Pacifies the North, and Governor of Southern Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (495), he was sent out as Bearer of the Staff, Area Commander of Southern Xu, General Who Pacifies the North, and Governor of Southern Xu.

sentences.zh: 東昏卽位，進征北大將軍，開府儀同三司，給扶。

translations.literal: When the Marquis of Donghun acceded, he was advanced to General Who Conquers the North, with an office staff equal to the Three Excellencies, and given a support staff.
translations.idiomatic: When the Marquis of Donghun took the throne, Bao Yi was promoted to General Who Conquers the North, granted an office staff equal to the Three Excellencies, and given attendants to support him.

sentences.zh: 永元元年，給班劔二十人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongyuan, he was given twenty halberd-bearers.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongyuan (499), he was granted twenty halberd-bearers as an escort.

sentences.zh: 始安王遙光誅，爲都督揚南徐二州軍事、驃騎大將軍、揚州刺史，持節如故。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Shi'an, Yaoguang, was executed, he became Supervisor of Military Affairs for Yang and Southern Xu, General of Agile Cavalry, and Governor of Yang Province, Bearer of Credentials as before.
translations.idiomatic: After the Prince of Shi'an, Yaoguang, was put to death, he was made Area Commander of Yang and Southern Xu, General of Agile Cavalry, and Governor of Yang Province, retaining his credentials as before.

sentences.zh: 東府被兵火，屋宇燒殘，帝方營宮殿，不暇脩葺，寶義鎮西州。

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace had suffered military fire; its buildings were burned to ruin. The emperor was then constructing palaces and had no leisure to repair them, so Bao Yi garrisoned the Western Quarter.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace had been ravaged by fire and its buildings left in ruins. The emperor was busy building new palaces and had no time to restore the old quarters, so Bao Yi was stationed in the Western Quarter.

sentences.zh: 三年，進位司徒。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was advanced to Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (499), he was promoted to Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 和帝西臺建，以爲侍中、司空，使持節、都督、刺史如故。

translations.literal: When the Western Terrace of Emperor He was established, he was made Palace Attendant and Minister of Works; Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor, and Governor remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor He's Western Terrace was set up, he was appointed Palace Attendant and Minister of Works, while his staff, area command, and governorship remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 梁王定京邑，宣德太后令以寶義爲太尉，領司徒。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Liang secured the capital, the Dowager Empress Xuande ordered that Bao Yi be made Grand Commandant and concurrently hold the post of Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: After the Prince of Liang secured the capital, Dowager Empress Xuande ordered Bao Yi appointed Grand Commandant while retaining the Ministry of Education.

sentences.zh: 詔云：「不言之化，形于自遠。」

translations.literal: The edict read: "Wordless transformation takes form from afar of itself."
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "His wordless transforming influence extends of itself even to the distance."

sentences.zh: 時人皆云此實錄也。

translations.literal: People of the time all said this was a faithful record.
translations.idiomatic: People at the time all said this was a truthful account.

sentences.zh: 梁受禪，封謝沐縣公，尋封巴陵郡王，奉齊後。

translations.literal: When Liang received the abdication, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Xiemu County; soon after he was enfeoffed as Prince of Baling Commandery to maintain the Qi succession.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang accepted the abdication, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Xiemu County, and soon after as Prince of Baling to preserve the Qi line.

sentences.zh: 天監中薨。

translations.literal: He died during the Tianjian era.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Tianjian reign (502–519).

sentences.zh: 江夏王寶玄字智深，明帝第三子也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jiangxia, Bao Xuan, style name Zhishen, was Emperor Ming's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xuan, Prince of Jiangxia, whose style name was Zhishen, was Emperor Ming's third son.

sentences.zh: 建武元年，爲征虜將軍，領石頭戍事，封江夏郡王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianwu he was made General Who Conquers the Barbarians, took charge of the Stone City garrison, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Jiangxia Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianwu (494) he was appointed General Who Conquers the Barbarians, placed in charge of the Stone City garrison, and enfeoffed as Prince of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 仍出爲持節、都督郢司二州軍事、西中郎將、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: He then went out as Bearer of Credentials, Supervisor of Military Affairs for the two provinces of E and Si, General of the West, and Governor of E.
translations.idiomatic: He was then sent out as Bearer of Credentials, Area Commander of E and Si, General of the West, and Governor of E.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，還爲前將軍，領石頭戍事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai he returned as General of the Van and took charge of the Stone City garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongtai (498) he was recalled as General of the Van and placed in charge of the Stone City garrison.

sentences.zh: 未拜，東昏卽位，進號鎮軍將軍。

translations.literal: Before he could accept the appointment, the Marquis of Donghun acceded and his title was advanced to General Who Guards the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, the Marquis of Donghun took the throne and Bao Xuan was promoted to General Who Guards the Army.

sentences.zh: 永元元年，又進車騎將軍，代晉安王寶義爲使持節、都督南徐兖二州軍事、南徐兖二州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongyuan he was further advanced to General of the Chariots and Cavalry and replaced the Prince of Jin'an, Bao Yi, as Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of Military Affairs for Southern Xu and Yan, and Governor of Southern Xu and Yan; his generalship remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongyuan (499) he was further promoted to General of the Chariots and Cavalry and replaced Bao Yi, Prince of Jin'an, as Bearer of the Staff, Area Commander of Southern Xu and Yan, and Governor of Southern Xu and Yan, retaining his rank as general.

sentences.zh: 寶玄娶尚書令徐孝嗣女爲妃，孝嗣被誅離絕，少帝送少姬二人與之，寶玄恨望，密有異計。

translations.literal: Bao Xuan married the daughter of Minister of Works Xu Xiaosi as his consort. When Xiaosi was executed they were separated; the young emperor sent him two junior consorts, and Bao Xuan, resentful and despairing, secretly harbored a different design.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xuan had taken as his consort the daughter of Director of the Imperial Secretariat Xu Xiaosi. After Xiaosi was executed they were separated, and the young emperor sent him two junior consorts in her place. Bao Xuan nursed resentment and secretly plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 明年，崔慧景舉兵，還至廣陵，遣使奉寶玄爲主。

translations.literal: The next year Cui Huijing raised troops and returned to Guangling, sending envoys to install Bao Xuan as leader.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Cui Huijing raised an army and marched back to Guangling, sending envoys to proclaim Bao Xuan their sovereign.

sentences.zh: 寶玄斬其使，因是發將吏防城。

translations.literal: Bao Xuan beheaded the envoys and on that account mobilized officers and clerks to defend the city.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xuan beheaded the envoys and thereupon mobilized his officers to fortify the city.

sentences.zh: 帝遣馬軍主戚平、外監黃林夫助鎮京口。

translations.literal: The emperor sent the cavalry commander Qi Ping and the outer supervisor Huang Linfu to help garrison Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the cavalry commander Qi Ping and the outer supervisor Huang Linfu to reinforce the garrison at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 慧景將渡江，寶玄密與相應，殺司馬孔矜、典籤呂承緒及平、林夫，開門納慧景。

translations.literal: As Huijing was about to cross the river, Bao Xuan secretly coordinated with him, killed the Chief Administrator Kong Jin and the registrar Lu Chengxu as well as Ping and Linfu, and opened the gates to admit Huijing.
translations.idiomatic: When Huijing was about to cross the Yangzi, Bao Xuan secretly colluded with him, killed Chief Administrator Kong Jin, registrar Lu Chengxu, and also Qi Ping and Huang Linfu, and opened the gates to admit Huijing's forces.

sentences.zh: 使長史沈佚之、諮議柳憕分部軍衆，乘八掆輿，手執絳麾幡，隨慧景至京師，住東城，百姓多往投集。

translations.literal: He sent the Chief Administrator Shen Yizhi and the Adviser Liu Kui to divide the army; riding an eight-pole palanquin and holding a crimson command banner in his hand, he followed Huijing to the capital, lodged in the Eastern City, and many common people went to join him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Chief Administrator Shen Yizhi and Adviser Liu Kui to deploy the troops. Riding an eight-pole palanquin and holding a crimson command banner, he followed Huijing to the capital, took up quarters in the Eastern City, and crowds of townspeople flocked to join him.

sentences.zh: 慧景敗，收得朝野投寶玄及慧景軍名，帝令燒之，曰：「江夏尚爾，豈復可罪餘人。」

translations.literal: When Huijing was defeated, lists were seized of those in court and countryside who had joined Bao Xuan and Huijing's army. The emperor ordered them burned, saying: "If Jiangxia is still like this, how can the rest be punished?"
translations.idiomatic: After Huijing's defeat, lists were seized of courtiers and commoners who had joined Bao Xuan and Huijing's army. The emperor ordered them burned, saying, "If even Jiangxia went so far, how can I punish anyone else?"

sentences.zh: 寶玄逃奔數日乃出。

translations.literal: Bao Xuan fled and hid for several days before coming forth.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xuan fled and hid for several days before surrendering.

sentences.zh: 帝召入後堂，以步鄣裹之，令羣小數十人鳴鼓角馳繞其外，遣人謂寶玄曰：「汝近圍我亦如此。」

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him into the rear hall, wrapped him in a screen of shields, and had several dozen lads beat drums and horns and gallop around outside, sending someone to tell Bao Xuan: "When you lately besieged me you did the same."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him to the rear hall, wrapped him in a shield enclosure, and had several dozen youths beat drums and horns and gallop around outside, then sent word to Bao Xuan: "When you lately besieged me, you did the same."

sentences.zh: 少日乃殺之。

translations.literal: A few days later he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later he was executed.

sentences.zh: 廬陵王寶源字智淵，明帝第五子也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Luling, Bao Yuan, style name Zhiyuan, was Emperor Ming's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Yuan, Prince of Luling, whose style name was Zhiyuan, was Emperor Ming's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 建武元年，爲北中郎將，鎮琅邪城，封廬陵郡王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianwu he was made General of the North, garrisoned Langya City, and enfeoffed as Prince of Luling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianwu (494) he was appointed General of the North, garrisoned Langya City, and enfeoffed as Prince of Luling.

sentences.zh: 遷右將軍，領石頭戍事，仍出爲使持節、都督南兖兖徐青冀五州軍事、後將軍、南兖州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Right, took charge of the Stone City garrison, and then went out as Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of Military Affairs for the five provinces of Southern Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, General of the Rear, and Governor of Southern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of the Right and placed in charge of the Stone City garrison, then sent out as Bearer of the Staff, Area Commander of Southern Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, General of the Rear, and Governor of Southern Yan.

sentences.zh: 王敬則伏誅，徙寶源爲都督會稽東陽臨海永嘉新安五郡軍事、會稽太守，將軍如故。

translations.literal: When Wang Jingze was executed, Bao Yuan was transferred to Supervisor of Military Affairs for the five commanderies of Kuaiji, Dongyang, Linhai, Yongjia, and Xin'an, and Governor of Kuaiji, his generalship remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Jingze was put to death, Bao Yuan was reassigned as Area Commander of Kuaiji, Dongyang, Linhai, Yongjia, and Xin'an and appointed Governor of Kuaiji, retaining his rank as general.

sentences.zh: 永元元年，進號安東將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongyuan his title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongyuan (499) he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 和帝卽位，以爲侍中、車騎將軍、開府儀同三司，都督、太守如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor He acceded, he was made Palace Attendant, General of the Chariots and Cavalry, and granted an office staff equal to the Three Excellencies; Supervisor and Governor remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor He took the throne, he was appointed Palace Attendant and General of the Chariots and Cavalry with an office staff equal to the Three Excellencies, while his area command and governorship remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 未拜，中興二年薨。

translations.literal: Before he could accept the appointment, he died in the second year of Zhongxing.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the appointment, he died in the second year of Zhongxing (502).

sentences.zh: 鄱陽王寶夤字智亮，明帝第六子也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Poyang, Bao Yin, style name Zhiliang, was Emperor Ming's sixth son.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Yin, Prince of Poyang, whose style name was Zhiliang, was Emperor Ming's sixth son.

sentences.zh: 建武初，封建安郡王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu he was enfeoffed as Prince of Jian'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianwu era he was enfeoffed as Prince of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 二年，爲北中郎將，鎮琅邪城。

translations.literal: In the second year he was made General of the North and garrisoned Langya City.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (495) he was appointed General of the North and garrisoned Langya City.

sentences.zh: 明年，出爲持節、都督江州軍事、南中郎將、江州刺史。

translations.literal: The next year he went out as Bearer of Credentials, Supervisor of Military Affairs for Jiang Province, General of the South, and Governor of Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was sent out as Bearer of Credentials, Area Commander of Jiang Province, General of the South, and Governor of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 東昏卽位，爲使持節、都督郢司二州軍事、征虜將軍、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Marquis of Donghun acceded, he was made Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of Military Affairs for the two provinces of E and Si, General Who Conquers the Barbarians, and Governor of E.
translations.idiomatic: When the Marquis of Donghun took the throne, he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Area Commander of E and Si, General Who Conquers the Barbarians, and Governor of E.

sentences.zh: 尋進號前將軍。

translations.literal: Soon his title was advanced to General of the Van.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to General of the Van.

sentences.zh: 永元二年，徵爲撫軍，領石頭戍事，未拜。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongyuan he was summoned as General Who Pacifies the Army and to take charge of the Stone City garrison, but did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongyuan (499) he was recalled as General Who Pacifies the Army and placed in charge of the Stone City garrison, but never took up the post.

sentences.zh: 三年，爲車騎將軍、開府儀同三司，鎮石頭。

translations.literal: In the third year he was made General of the Chariots and Cavalry with an office staff equal to the Three Excellencies and garrisoned Stone City.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (500) he was appointed General of the Chariots and Cavalry with an office staff equal to the Three Excellencies and garrisoned Stone City.

sentences.zh: 其秋，雍州刺史張欣泰等謀起事於新亭，殺臺內諸主帥，事在欣泰傳。

translations.literal: That autumn the Governor of Yong Province Zhang Xintai and others plotted to raise a revolt at Xinting and kill the various commanders within the capital; the affair is set forth in Xintai's biography.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Zhang Xintai, Governor of Yong, and others plotted an uprising at Xinting to kill the capital's chief commanders; the affair is recorded in Xintai's biography.

sentences.zh: 難作之日，前南譙太守王靈秀奔往石頭，率城內將吏見力，去車脚載寶夤向臺城，百姓數千人皆空手隨後，京邑騷亂。

translations.literal: On the day the trouble broke out, the former Governor of Southern Qiao Wang Lingxiu fled to Stone City, led the officers and clerks within the city and the men on hand, removed the carriage shafts, and carried Bao Yin toward the Palace City; several thousand common people followed behind empty-handed, and the capital was thrown into turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: When the crisis erupted, the former Governor of Southern Qiao Wang Lingxiu rushed to Stone City, rallied the city's officers and available troops, stripped a carriage to its poles, and bore Bao Yin toward the Palace City. Several thousand townspeople followed behind empty-handed, and the capital fell into uproar.

sentences.zh: 寶夤至杜姥宅，日已欲暗，城門閉，城上人射之，衆棄寶夤逃走。

translations.literal: Bao Yin reached Old Lady Du's residence; the day was nearly dark, the city gates were closed, and men on the walls shot at them; the crowd abandoned Bao Yin and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Yin reached Old Lady Du's quarter as dusk was falling. The city gates were shut, defenders on the walls shot at them, and the crowd abandoned Bao Yin and fled.

sentences.zh: 寶夤逃亡三日，戎服詣草市尉，尉馳以啓帝，帝迎寶夤入宮問之。

translations.literal: Bao Yin fled for three days, then in military dress went to the Grass Market commandant; the commandant galloped to report to the emperor, and the emperor received Bao Yin into the palace to question him.
translations.idiomatic: After three days in hiding, Bao Yin appeared at the Grass Market commandant's office in military dress. The commandant galloped to report to the emperor, who received Bao Yin in the palace to question him.

sentences.zh: 寶夤涕泣稱：「爾日不知何人逼使上車，仍將去，制不自由。」

translations.literal: Bao Yin wept and said: "That day I did not know who forced me into the carriage and carried me off; I was not free to control myself."
translations.idiomatic: Bao Yin wept and said, "That day I did not know who forced me into the carriage and carried me off against my will."

sentences.zh: 帝笑，乃復爵位。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and then restored his rank and fief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and restored his titles.

sentences.zh: 和帝立，西臺以寶夤爲使持節、都督南徐兖二州軍事、衞將軍、南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor He was established, the Western Terrace made Bao Yin Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of Military Affairs for Southern Xu and Yan, General of the Guard, and Governor of Southern Xu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor He was enthroned, the Western Terrace appointed Bao Yin Bearer of the Staff, Area Commander of Southern Xu and Yan, General of the Guard, and Governor of Southern Xu.

sentences.zh: 少帝以爲使持節、都督荊益寧雍梁南北秦七州軍事、荊州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: The young emperor made him Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of Military Affairs for the seven provinces of Jing, Yi, Ning, Yong, Liang, and Northern and Southern Qin, and Governor of Jing; his generalship remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: The young emperor appointed him Bearer of the Staff, Area Commander of Jing, Yi, Ning, Yong, Liang, and Northern and Southern Qin, and Governor of Jing, while retaining his rank as general.

sentences.zh: 宣德太后臨朝，梁王爲建安公，改封寶夤爲鄱陽王。

translations.literal: When the Dowager Empress Xuande held court, the Prince of Liang was made Duke of Jian'an, and Bao Yin's enfeoffment was changed to Prince of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Dowager Empress Xuande held court, the Prince of Liang was made Duke of Jian'an, and Bao Yin was reassigned as Prince of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 中興二年，謀反誅。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongxing he plotted rebellion and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongxing (502) he plotted rebellion and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 邵陵王寶攸字智宣，明帝第九子也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Shaoling, Bao You, style name Zhixuan, was Emperor Ming's ninth son.
translations.idiomatic: Bao You, Prince of Shaoling, whose style name was Zhixuan, was Emperor Ming's ninth son.

sentences.zh: 建武元年，封南平郡王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianwu he was enfeoffed as Prince of Nanping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianwu (494) he was enfeoffed as Prince of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 二年，改封。

translations.literal: In the second year his enfeoffment was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (495) his enfeoffment was changed.

sentences.zh: 三年，爲北中郎將，鎮琅邪城。

translations.literal: In the third year he was made General of the North and garrisoned Langya City.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (496) he was appointed General of the North and garrisoned Langya City.

sentences.zh: 永元元年，爲持節、都督南北徐南兖青冀五州軍事、南兖州刺史，郎將如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongyuan he was made Bearer of Credentials, Supervisor of Military Affairs for the five provinces of Northern and Southern Xu, Southern Yan, Qing, and Ji, and Governor of Southern Yan; his rank as commander remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongyuan (499) he was appointed Bearer of Credentials, Area Commander of Northern and Southern Xu, Southern Yan, Qing, and Ji, and Governor of Southern Yan, retaining his rank as commander.

sentences.zh: 未拜，遷征虜將軍，領石頭戍事。

translations.literal: Before he could accept the appointment, he was transferred to General Who Conquers the Barbarians and took charge of the Stone City garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, he was reassigned as General Who Conquers the Barbarians and placed in charge of the Stone City garrison.

sentences.zh: 丹楊尹，戍事如故。

translations.literal: He was made Governor of Danyang; his garrison duties remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Governor of Danyang while retaining his garrison duties.

sentences.zh: 陳顯達事平，出爲持節、督江州軍事、左將軍、江州刺史。

translations.literal: When Chen Xianda's affair was settled, he went out as Bearer of Credentials, Supervisor of Military Affairs for Jiang Province, General of the Left, and Governor of Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen Xianda's rebellion was suppressed, he was sent out as Bearer of Credentials, Area Commander of Jiang Province, General of the Left, and Governor of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 以本號還京師，授中軍將軍，祕書監。

translations.literal: With his former title he returned to the capital and was given the posts of General of the Central Army and Superintendent of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital with his former title and was appointed General of the Central Army and Director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 中興二年，謀反，宣德太后令賜死。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongxing he plotted rebellion, and Dowager Empress Xuande ordered him granted death.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongxing (502) he plotted rebellion, and Dowager Empress Xuande ordered him put to death.

sentences.zh: 晉熙王寶嵩字智靖，明帝第十子也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jinxing, Bao Song, style name Zhijing, was Emperor Ming's tenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Song, Prince of Jinxing, whose style name was Zhijing, was Emperor Ming's tenth son.

sentences.zh: 永元二年，爲冠軍將軍、丹楊尹。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongyuan he was made General Who Conquers Champions and Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongyuan (500) he was appointed General Who Conquers Champions and Governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 仍遷持節、都督南徐兖二州軍事、南徐州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was then transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of Military Affairs for Southern Xu and Yan, and Governor of Southern Xu; his generalship remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was then reassigned as Bearer of the Staff, Area Commander of Southern Xu and Yan, and Governor of Southern Xu, retaining his rank as general.

sentences.zh: 中興元年，和帝以爲中書令。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongxing Emperor He made him Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongxing (501) Emperor He appointed him Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明年，謀反伏誅。

translations.literal: The next year he plotted rebellion and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he plotted rebellion and was executed.

sentences.zh: 桂陽王寶貞，明帝第十一子也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Guiyang, Bao Zhen, was Emperor Ming's eleventh son.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Zhen, Prince of Guiyang, was Emperor Ming's eleventh son.

sentences.zh: 永元二年，爲中護軍、北中郎將，領石頭戍事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongyuan he was made General of the Palace Guard, General of the North, and took charge of the Stone City garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongyuan (499) he was appointed General of the Palace Guard and General of the North, and placed in charge of the Stone City garrison.

sentences.zh: 中興二年，謀反伏誅。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongxing he plotted rebellion and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongxing (502) he plotted rebellion and was executed.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：《春秋》書「鄭伯克段于鄢」，兄弟之恩離，君臣之義正。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 records, "The Duke of Zheng defeated Duan at Yan"—the bond between brothers was sundered, and the principle between ruler and subject was set right.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer remarks: The 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 records that "the Duke of Zheng defeated Duan at Yan"—thereby sundering the bond of brotherhood and upholding the principle between ruler and subject.

sentences.zh: 夫逆從有勢，況親兼一體，道窮數盡，或容觸啄。

translations.literal: For rebellion and obedience each has its momentum; how much more when kin share one body—when the Way is exhausted and fate spent, one may perhaps allow a pecking clash.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion and loyalty each follow their own momentum; how much more when kin share one flesh—when the Way is spent and fate exhausted, a clash of beaks may yet be tolerated.

sentences.zh: 而寶玄自尋干戈，欣受家難。

translations.literal: Yet Bao Xuan himself sought out weapons of war and gladly welcomed calamity within the family.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Bao Xuan took up arms of his own accord and welcomed the ruin of his own house.

sentences.zh: 曾不悟執柯所指，跗蕚相從，以此而圖萬全，未知其髣髴也。

translations.literal: He never understood that the axe-handle points the way and the calyx and petals follow one another; to seek complete security on this basis shows he did not even grasp the likeness.
translations.idiomatic: He never understood that the axe-handle shows the way and calyx and petals must follow together; to seek perfect safety on such terms was to mistake the very likeness of things.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：文惠二王，于嗟夭殤。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Wen Hui's two princes—alas, they died young.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: Wen Hui's two princes—alas, cut off in youth.

sentences.zh: 明子七國，終亦衰亡。

translations.literal: Ming's seven sons and their states in the end also declined and perished.
translations.idiomatic: Ming's seven princely lines likewise ended in ruin.

translations.literal: [1] Endnote marker.
translations.idiomatic: [1] Endnote marker.
